## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR shouldn't merge yet. When a bare `--json` comes before another flag, the parser takes that flag as the JSON path. So the combination this PR is meant to support, the default JSON destination together with `--junit`, either fails or writes JSON to a file named after the flag.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — When `--json` is followed by any token, that token becomes the JSON path, even if it is a flag. With `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])`, the parser sets `options["json"] = "--junit"`, then treats `out.xml` as a flag and raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. With `["--json", "--junit"]`, it returns `{"json": "--junit"}`, and `write_reports` then creates a file named `--junit`. This also contradicts the comment at line 12, "JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied". Could you guard lines 15 and 18 with `not args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, the same check `--junit` uses at line 7? Please also add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]`, since `tests/test_cli.py:7` only tests `--json` on its own. — If a user puts a bare `--json` before `--junit`, the run either aborts with a misleading "unknown option" error or writes the JSON report to a stray `--junit` file and never writes the JUnit report.
